blockers: Needs written, customer-consumable DR plan for VPC single-region and guidance to expand to multi-AZ; wants clear RPO/RTO commitments (not just best-effort).
Security wants confirmation backups are encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS) and clarity on key rotation + behavior during KMS outages.
Wants deterministic restore procedure with validation checklist (smoke tests) and a sample game day / drill cadence they can operationalize.
Clarify what is backed up vs out of scope (e.g., Kubernetes resources/CRDs, data plane state) to avoid gaps in regulator review.
Procurement: needs artifact signing / integrity verification story for any offline tooling used in restricted environments (they may enforce limited egress even in VPC).
company_overview_notes: Enterprise banking account. Interested in Redwood Private in a dedicated VPC with strict operational controls. Primary driver is predictable latency + ability to operate under internal security standards. They are evaluating vendors based on DR readiness and evidence (runbooks, validation reports) as much as model performance.
deployment_notes: Target: Redwood Private in AWS VPC (single-region initially). Preference for multi-AZ control plane pattern if supported. Restricted outbound egress (not fully air-gapped, but expects no dependency on public endpoints during restore). Wants backups to land in customer-owned S3 with CMEK (KMS) and tight IAM (least privilege).
requirements_summary: RPO/RTO: they asked for component-level targets rather than a single number. Early asks: config/control-plane state RPO <= 15m, RTO 2-4h for a clean-cluster restore in-region. Audit logs: retention/export requirements for evidence and incident reconstruction. Wants restore to be repeatable, documented, and testable via periodic drills (prefer monthly in non-prod, quarterly in prod).
model_and_workload_notes: Workloads: internal knowledge assistant + summarization of customer communications and case notes. Mix of chat + retrieval + reranking. Latency sensitivity: interactive UX target p95 under 2s end-to-end for typical prompts; throughput bursts during business hours. Strong preference for pinned model versions and rollback/fallback policies.
security_and_compliance_notes: Security review emphasized: (1) encryption at rest for backup artifacts with customer-managed keys, (2) audit logging and retention/export controls, (3) clear separation between secret material vs secret references in backups, (4) evidence artifacts post-drill (restore report, timestamps, checksums, operator identity). Asked: 'If KMS is down, do backups fail closed?' and 'How do we rotate keys without breaking restores?'
decision_process_notes: Stakeholders: platform engineering + infrastructure reliability + security/compliance. Buying criteria include DR runbooks, restore validation automation, and clarity on what support will handle vs what customer must operate. They requested a mutual action plan with dates for: draft runbooks, a staged restore drill, and sign-off from security.
